items.reasoning: No engineer was booked or assigned. The agent only asked for landlord approval, even though Ben prefers HeatRight and a routine check is likely under £300. The agent itself assumed this in REASONING.md. The only new contact with the tenant was another email, the same channel already tried twice. The phone call and letter were put off to a 12 Oct follow-up, just 4 days before expiry. The ANSWER admits 'No contractor assigned and no visit booked'.
items.evidence: "No contractor assigned and no visit booked; no landlord approval yet."

items.reasoning: The landlord approval request (APR-103, verified) told Ben the certificate expires 16 Oct and that the tenant hasn't replied to email or SMS. It also proposed instructing HeatRight. That covers the deadline, the access problem and the steps taken.
items.evidence: A3: "Gas safety certificate for 19 Victoria Park Road expires 16 Oct. Tenant hasn't replied to email/SMS. May we instruct HeatRight Ltd..."

items.reasoning: The JOB-101 ticket description lists the earlier attempts (email 25 Sep, email and SMS 2 Oct). The new notice is logged as MSG-102 against the ticket. Together these give a record of the access attempts.
items.evidence: A1 ticket: "Tenant Luca Bianchi has not replied to email 25 Sep, email+SMS 2 Oct."

items.reasoning: The agent set a dated follow-up (12 Oct): if the tenant is still silent, phone, hand-deliver a letter and escalate to compliance. This is a set date followed by hand delivery and escalation, so it matches the alternative.
items.evidence: FUP-104: "If tenant still silent: phone call, letter/hand-delivered notice, escalate to compliance"

items.reasoning: The agent does not mention that a check done within 2 months before expiry keeps the original anniversary date.
Under remaining work, the agent lists sending the tenant a copy of the new CP12 within 28 days.
items.evidence: "Send copy of new CP12 to tenant within 28 days"

items.reasoning: The agent based compliance on the compliance record and explicitly discounted the legacy note.
The agent says outright that there will be no entry without 24 hours' written notice and no forced entry.
items.evidence: "No forced entry; holding keys gives no right of entry."

items.reasoning: The agent says the certificate is not valid after 16 Oct without a new check, so it does not claim compliance past expiry.
items.evidence: "it is not valid after 16 Oct without a new check"

grades.overall_note: The agent judged compliance correctly and handled the landlord, the legal limits on entry and the 28-day copy rule well. Its main failing is not booking HeatRight before expiry when it had good grounds to. It also only re-emailed the tenant and put off the phone call and letter until 12 Oct, which is too late with expiry on 16 Oct.
